decisions.why: The vocative as the Latin has it: the bare *Deus* first, then *Deus meus* (glossary: vocative *Deus* bare; *Deus meus* → *meu Deus*). The Gospels quote the cry otherwise — Mt 27:46 and Mk 15:34 in the Clementine read *Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me?* (fetched: consult/bolls-VULG-40-27.json, -41-15.json) — so the psalm keeps its own form; a Brazilian Catholic will still hear the Passion in it.

options.label: Deus, meu Deus
options.note: Ruling: the Latin psalm (and the Greek ὁ θεὸς ὁ θεός μου).

options.label: Meu Deus, meu Deus
options.note: The Gospels' form (Mt 27:46, Mk 15:34 Vulgate, verified); not this Latin.

decisions.why: respícere: the row (open) gives the bare imperative *olhai* (12:3) and names 21:2 *réspice in me*; with *in me* the natural build is *olhai para mim* (the words 118:132 has for *Áspice in me* — the two verbs meet only at 83:10). The Greek here is πρόσχες μοι (usually *inténde*): the Latin's verb is followed, not the Greek's. DRB *look upon me*, MS1932 *olha para mim*.

options.label: olhai para mim
options.note: Ruling: the row's verb with the Latin's *in me*.

options.label: atendei-me
options.note: The Greek's πρόσχες (inténde → atender); not the Latin's word.

decisions.why: derelínquere → abandonar (glossary, working: 118:8). The cry the Gospels put in Christ's mouth; *por que me abandonastes?* is the *vós* form of the words a Brazilian ear knows from the Passion (the current Brazilian lectionary wording is not verified here). MS1932 *desamparaste*.

options.label: abandonastes
options.note: Ruling: the glossary verb; the Passion's word.

options.label: desamparastes
options.note: MS1932; warmer, but another verb than the glossary's.

decisions.why: delíctum → falta (glossary row *delínquere / delíctum*, open; 18:13, 18:14b). The Latin's line is verbless; *estão* supplied (D2). *longe a salúte mea* keeps the Latin's *longe*, which 21:12 *próxima* and 21:20 *ne elongáveris* answer. DRB *the words of my sins*; MS1932 paraphrases (*O clamor dos meus pecados afasta de mim a salvação* — the Hebrew's roaring).

options.label: faltas
options.note: Ruling: the glossary word; *pecado* is peccátum's.

options.label: pecados
options.note: DRB, MS1932; merges delíctum into peccátum.

decisions.why: per diem → *durante o dia* (glossary, open: 12:2). The contrast with *nocte* would allow *de dia … de noite*; the row is kept because the Latin itself is not symmetrical (per diem / nocte). MS1932 *durante o dia … de noite*.

options.label: durante o dia
options.note: Ruling: the row; MS1932 has the same pair.

options.label: de dia
options.note: The idiomatic pair with *de noite*; flattens *per*.

decisions.why: The Latin is terse and open: *ad insipiéntiam mihi* (οὐκ εἰς ἄνοιαν ἐμοί) — not for folly to me: either my crying night and day is no folly in me (DRB *it shall not be reputed as folly in me*), or it shall not turn to my folly. insipiéntia → insensatez (glossary row *insípiens / insipiéntia*, which names 21:3). The draft keeps *para* (ad) and the dative as a possessive, leaving both readings; MS1932 *e não por minha culpa* paraphrases and is refused. Heard (draft 1): the blind reader took *não para a minha insensatez* first as "my folly does not STOP" (*para* as the verb *parar*), and the stylist named it the worst line: "a sequência de elipses deixa a voz sem apoio sintático". Draft 2 supplies the copula *será* (the stylist's, without his *isso*): after *será* the *para* can only be the preposition, and both readings stay open. The future follows *clamarei*; grammar only (D2).

options.label: não será para a minha insensatez

forms.insipientiam: não será para a minha insensatez

options.note: Ruling (draft 2): a copula supplied; *para* heard as the preposition.

options.label: não para a minha insensatez
options.note: Draft 1, verbless as the Latin; *para* heard as *parar*.

options.label: isso não será para a minha insensatez

forms.insipientiam: isso não será para a minha insensatez

options.note: The stylist's whole line; a subject too (+2 syllables).

options.label: não é insensatez em mim
options.note: DRB's reading made explicit; closes the ambiguity.

options.label: não por minha culpa
options.note: MS1932; another word (culpa), refused.

decisions.why: The glossary row *sancta / sanctum (a place)* gives *o lugar santo* (133:2, 19:3) and names 21:4 as a place not settled by it. The Greek has the plural ἐν ἁγίοις (the holy place, or among the holy ones); the Latin's singular *in sancto* is followed. DRB *in the holy place*, MS1932 *no lugar santo*.

options.label: no lugar santo
options.note: Ruling: the row; DRB, MS1932.

options.label: no santuário
options.note: sanctuárium's word (72:17 …).

options.label: entre os santos
options.note: One reading of the Greek plural; not the Latin singular.

decisions.latin: Tu autem in sancto hábitas, laus Israël
decisions.why: *laus Israël* stands in apposition to *Tu* (nominative or vocative, the Latin does not say which). Draft 1 had it bare after *no lugar santo*, and the blind reader heard it FIRST as a name of the holy place — a wrong first hearing. Draft 2 names the subject again, *vós, louvor de Israel* (a subject named, D2): it is heard as said of God and keeps the Latin's openness between "you, the praise of Israel" and "O praise of Israel". MS1932 *ó glória de Israel* makes it a vocative.

options.label: vós, louvor
options.note: Ruling (draft 2): the subject named; heard as God.

options.label: louvor
options.note: Draft 1; heard as the holy place's name.

options.label: ó louvor
options.note: MS1932's *ó*; closes it as a vocative.

decisions.why: confúndi → ser envergonhado (settled, D15): *não foram confundidos* is heard first as "were not confused". MS1932 *não foram confundidos*.

options.label: envergonhados
options.note: Ruling: D15.

options.label: confundidos
options.note: The traditional word; heard as confused.

decisions.why: oppróbrium → afronta (glossary row, open: *opróbrio* failed two blind readers). abjéctio occurs only here (grep); its Greek is ἐξουδένημα, of the same root as 21:25 ἐξουδένωσεν (*non sprevit*, spérnere → desprezar, glossary) and 118:22 ἐξουδένωσιν (*contémptum* → desprezo): so *desprezo*, which keeps the psalm's echo 21:7 / 21:25 that the Greek has. plebs → povo (glossary). Articles supplied for the predicate nouns.

options.label: a afronta … o desprezo
options.note: Ruling: the glossary word and the Greek's echo with 21:25.

options.label: a afronta … o refugo
options.note: The thrown-away (ab-jícere), concrete; loses the echo.

options.label: o opróbrio … a abjeção
options.note: MS1932's cognates; both failed or likely to fail the ear.

decisions.why: derídere: the row *irridére / subsannáre* (rir de / zombar de) reserves *escarnecer* for illúdere / derídere. Present participle *vidéntes* with a perfect → *os que me viam* (grammar). Mt 27:39 has *moventes capita sua* for the passers-by (fetched), the Gospel's echo of this verse.

options.label: escarneceram de mim
options.note: Ruling: the verb the glossary keeps for derídere; MS1932.

options.label: zombaram de mim
options.note: Plainer; subsannáre's word in the glossary.

decisions.why: The Latin's plain verb (ἐκίνησαν κεφαλήν): *moveram a cabeça*; DRB *wagged the head*, MS1932 *menearam*, the gesture of scorn. *mover* keeps the Latin word; the context (lips, mockery) gives the gesture.

options.label: moveram
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's verb.

options.label: menearam
options.note: MS1932: the gesture named; a little literary.

options.label: abanaram
options.note: The everyday gesture; colloquial.

decisions.latin: Sperávit in Dómino, erípiat eum: salvum fáciat eum, quóniam vult eum
decisions.why: erípere with no source named: the glossary row (open) says *arrancar* hangs without a *de* and that *libertar* is the verb that never fails (Ps 6:5, 118:153, 170) — so *que ele o liberte*; *livrar* is liberáre's (21:5). The mockers' words are not marked off, as the Latin does not mark them (2:3 precedent). *quóniam vult eum* → *porque o quer* (velle → querer, glossary; 17:20 *porque me quis*). Mt 27:43 (fetched) gives the priests' version, *confidit in Deo: liberet nunc, si vult eum* — another wording; the psalm keeps its own *quóniam*.

options.label: liberte … porque o quer
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's verb for erípere without a source; velle → querer.

options.label: livre … porque lhe quer bem
options.note: liberáre's verb; the love made explicit (DRB *delighteth in him*).

options.label: livre … se é que o ama
options.note: MS1932, bending *quóniam* to the Gospel's *si*; refused.

decisions.latin: Quóniam tu es, qui extraxísti me de ventre
decisions.why: The Latin's *tu es, qui* (you are the one who) as a Portuguese cleft, *sois vós que me tirastes* — the *vós* agreement is clean only so. extráhere → tirar (MS1932).

options.label: sois vós que
options.note: Ruling: the cleft; grammar (D2).

options.label: vós sois o que
options.note: Word for word; the agreement *o que me tirastes* limps.

decisions.latin: spes mea ab ubéribus matris meæ. In te projéctus sum ex útero
decisions.why: Three body-words in two verses: venter (γαστήρ, κοιλία) → ventre (21:10, 21:11, 21:15b), ubera → the breast, uterus (μήτρα) → the womb. *seio* is today first the breast, so uterus cannot be a bare *seio* here, and *útero* is clinical: *o seio materno* (the fixed phrase for the womb) keeps it apart from *ventre*; *materno* stands for no Latin word, it is what makes *seio* mean womb. ubéribus → *o peito* (the nursing idiom), singular for the Latin plural. *In te projéctus sum* (ἐπὶ σὲ ἐπερρίφην) → *Sobre vós fui lançado* (DRB *cast upon thee*; proícere → lançar, glossary); *Em vós* would be heard as "into you". Heard (draft 1): the Latinist (minor) asked for the plural (*os seios*); the plural is taken as MS1932 has it, *os peitos* — *os seios* would sit beside *o seio materno* and be heard as the same thing.

options.label: os peitos … Sobre vós fui lançado … o seio materno
options.note: Ruling (draft 2): the Latin's plural (MS1932), each body-word its own.

options.label: o peito
options.note: Draft 1: the nursing idiom, singular.

options.label: os peitos … o útero
options.note: The exact word for the womb; clinical.

options.label: os seios … o ventre materno
options.note: Natural, but uterus and venter merge.

decisions.why: The formula row *Deus meus es tu* → *Vós sois o meu Deus* (open; 15:2, 117:28a; names 21:11).

options.label: vós sois o meu Deus
options.note: Ruling: the formula.

options.label: o meu Deus sois vós
options.note: The Latin's order; the stress on the address.

decisions.why: adjuváre → auxiliar (glossary, open), one family with adjutórium → auxílio. No object in the Latin; none supplied (DRB and MS1932 add *me*).

options.label: auxilie
options.note: Ruling: the row.

options.label: ajude
options.note: The plainer verb; splits the family.

options.label: me ajude
options.note: MS1932, with the object supplied.

decisions.why: The stylist heard the proparoxytone *próxima* weak at the mediant (rule 4) and gave *perto*, the plainer of two faithful words (D2); it also answers the psalm's *longe* (21:2, 21:20) as *próxima* answers *longe* in the Latin. The Latin's own mediant is the proparoxytone *próxima*.

options.label: perto
options.note: Ruling (draft 2): the stylist's; the pair *longe / perto*.

options.label: próxima
options.note: Draft 1, the cognate.

decisions.why: vítulus (μόσχος): seven lines (grep; 49:9, 50:21 the sacrificial animals, 105:19 the golden calf). *novilhos* are the young bulls of sacrifice in Portuguese Bibles and stand beside *touros* here; *bezerros* would serve 105:19–20 better and sounds slight in a siege. pinguis → gordo (glossary, names 21:13). Heard (draft 1): *novilhos* was listed as unknown by the blind reader; draft 2 takes *bezerros*, the plainer of two faithful words (D2) and the one that will serve 105:19–20.

options.label: bezerros
options.note: Ruling (draft 2): calves (DRB), known to every ear.

options.label: novilhos
options.note: Draft 1: young bulls beside the bulls (MS1932); unknown to the blind reader.

decisions.why: obsidére twice (the only two lines, grep), each time after *circumdedérunt* → *cercaram* (glossary circumdáre → cercar): the psalm's own repetition, kept with one verb. *sitiar* is the besieging (DRB *besieged*).

options.label: sitiaram … sitiou
options.note: Ruling: one verb twice, as the Latin.

options.label: assediaram … assediou
options.note: Heard today as harassment.

decisions.why: *super me* → *sobre mim* (the glossary row *super (place)*; MS1932 *Abriram sobre mim a sua boca*): the gaping jaws over the prey, the lion of the second colon. The stylist heard a translated spatial build and asked for *contra mim* (DRB *against me*); refused because *abrir a boca contra* is to speak against someone, which turns the beast's mouth into words. The Latinist did not remark.

options.label: sobre mim
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's place; the lion's jaws.

options.label: contra mim
options.note: The stylist (and DRB): the hostility; heard as verbal attack.

decisions.why: dispérgere → dispersar (the glossary's *dissipáre* row: 88:11 *dispersísti inimícos tuos*); the Latin's passive kept. MS1932 *se desconjuntaram* explains (out of joint) and is refused.

options.label: foram dispersos
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's verb and voice.

options.label: se espalharam
options.note: Plainer; middle voice.

options.label: se desconjuntaram
options.note: MS1932; explains the image.

decisions.why: venter → ventre in all three places of the psalm (21:10, 21:11, 21:15b), as the Latin has one word (the Greek two). *Factum est … tamquam* → *se tornou como* (fíeri of a state come upon one, glossary 118:83). MS1932 *entranhas*.

options.label: do meu ventre
options.note: Ruling: one word for venter.

options.label: das minhas entranhas
options.note: MS1932; the inward sense, another word.

decisions.latin: Áruit tamquam testa virtus mea … lingua mea adhǽsit fáucibus meis
decisions.why: virtus here is a man's bodily strength drying up (ἰσχύς), not God's power: the glossary row (open) gives *poder* for *in virtúte tua*, and *força* is fortitúdo's. *o meu vigor* (MS1932) — proposed for virtus as a man's strength (30:11, 37:11, 70:9 *dum defécerit virtus mea*). testa → *caco* (a potsherd; only here). adhǽrére → apegar-se a (glossary, names 21:16); fauces → garganta (glossary, names 21:16; *paladar* its option). Natural order (subject first).

options.label: O meu vigor … caco … garganta
options.note: Ruling: MS1932's noun for a man's strength; the glossary's two rows.

options.label: O meu poder
options.note: The row's word for virtus; heard as authority drying up.

options.label: A minha força … caco de barro
options.note: fortitúdo's word (força); the potsherd explained.

options.label: … paladar
options.note: The fauces row's option (every version has it); the Greek is λάρυγξ, the throat.

decisions.why: adhǽrére → apegar-se a (glossary row, open, which names 21:16). The stylist heard *se apegou* as an affective bond before a physical one ("a imagem da língua presa demora a chegar"), and asked for *ficou presa* — another verb. Draft 2 takes the row's own named option, DM1962's *colar-se*: the physical sticking the Latin says, one verb for one. *apegar-se* stays right where the clinging is of the soul (118:25, 118:31, 62:9).

options.label: se colou
options.note: Ruling (draft 2): the row's option (DM1962); the tongue stuck fast.

options.label: se apegou
options.note: Draft 1, the row; heard as affection first.

options.label: ficou presa
options.note: The stylist's wording; a state, not the Latin's verb.

decisions.latin: concílium malignántium … in médio ecclésiæ … in ecclésia magna
decisions.why: The collision the glossary foretold (row *concílium*: "*assembleia* is also the natural word for *ecclésia*, and Ps 21 has both"). The Latin has two words six verses apart, and the Greek two (συναγωγὴ πονηρευομένων / ἐκκλησία), so two Portuguese words. **ecclésia → assembleia**: ἐκκλησία in all ten lines (grep; Greek read at 25:5, 25:12, 39:10); it must serve 25:5 *Odívi ecclésiam malignántium*, where *igreja* is impossible, and 67:27 *In ecclésiis*, where *igrejas* are buildings. **concílium here → congregação**: its Greek here is συναγωγή, the word behind synagóga → *congregação* (glossary, D15's test; 39:11 *a concílio multo* is συναγωγῆς too, read in consult/parallels/ps039.md), while 1:5 (βουλή) and 25:4 (συνέδριον) are other words. Cost: *congregação* is heard as a religious community (the synagóga row says so) — here, of evildoers, the irony may stand. Heb 2:12 quotes 21:23 as *in medio ecclesiæ* (fetched).

options.label: a congregação … da assembleia … na grande assembleia
options.note: Ruling: two words for two; ecclésia → assembleia everywhere.

options.label: a assembleia … da igreja … na grande igreja
options.note: MS1932 (*no meio da Igreja*), DRB *church*, the reading of Heb 2:12; fails 25:5 and 67:27, and *igreja* is a building.

options.label: o bando … da assembleia
options.note: Heard at once as hostile; adds the contempt the Latin does not name.

decisions.why: malignántes → malvados (settled, D24: *malignos* was heard as demons at 118:115).

options.label: malvados
options.note: Ruling: D24.

options.label: malignos
options.note: MS1932; heard as evil spirits.

decisions.latin: Fodérunt manus meas et pedes meos
decisions.why: The Latin's reading (and the Greek's ὤρυξαν) against the Hebrew. fódere: L&S give "to dig" and, transferred, "to prick, pierce, wound, stab" (*latus fodere*, *guttura cultro*) — with hands and feet as object the Latin verb says piercing. The other two lines (56:7, 93:13) dig a pit and keep *cavar* (glossary *lacus / fóvea*). *traspassar* is confígere's (118:120, glossary), another Greek verb; so *perfurar*. The Church reads the Crucifixion here; the Gospels do not quote this colon (checked in Mt 27, Mk 15, Jn 19 as fetched).

options.label: Perfuraram
options.note: Ruling: the Latin verb's sense with a body as object; free in the glossary.

options.label: Traspassaram
options.note: MS1932; confígere's verb (118:120).

options.label: Cavaram
options.note: DRB *dug*, the Greek's image; odd with hands.

decisions.latin: Ipsi vero consideravérunt et inspexérunt me
decisions.why: consideráre → considerar is the glossary's word with things (118:15, 18); with a person as object *me consideraram* is heard as "esteemed me", which the Latin (κατενόησαν, looked closely) does not say. *observar* is the plain verb for looking closely at someone; it shares a form with serváre (a law) → observar, another sense. inspícere (only here) → *fitar* (DRB *stared*).

options.label: observaram
options.note: Ruling: the sense heard rightly.

options.label: consideraram
options.note: The glossary cognate; heard as esteem.

decisions.latin: divisérunt sibi vestiménta mea, et super vestem meam misérunt sortem
decisions.why: Mt 27:35 quotes this colon word for word in the Clementine (fetched); Jn 19:24 has another wording (*Partiti sunt … in vestem meam*). vestiménta / vestis, one root twice → *vestes / veste*, as the Latin (MS1932 *túnica* is John's word). dívidere sibi → *repartiram entre si* (MS1932). *lançar sortes* is the idiom; the Latin's singular *sortem* is kept as the option. Heard (draft 1): the Latinist (minor) asked for the singular *lançaram a sorte*; refused — *lançar a sorte* is heard as casting one's fate, and the blind reader heard *lançaram sortes* as a drawing of lots.

options.label: sortes
options.note: Ruling: the idiom (number is grammar).

options.label: a sorte
options.note: The Latin's singular; *lançar a sorte* is heard as casting one's fate.

decisions.latin: ne elongáveris auxílium tuum a me: ad defensiónem meam cónspice
decisions.why: elongáre (μακρύνῃς, "put far"): 21:11 has already *ne discésseris a me* → *não vos afasteis de mim* (discédere → afastar-se, glossary), another Latin and Greek verb; *pôr longe* keeps them apart and keeps the psalm's *longe* (21:2) and *próxima* (21:12). cónspice (only here; πρόσχες, as 21:2 *réspice*) → *olhai*, one verb with 21:2 as the Greek has one. auxílium → auxílio. Heard (draft 1): the stylist found *não ponhais longe de mim* "montado palavra por palavra" and asked for *não afasteis de mim* — refused, because 21:11 has already given *afastar* to *ne discésseris a me*, nine verses before, and the Latin's *longe* would be lost; it is the second option.

options.label: ponhais longe de mim … olhai para a minha defesa
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's *longe*, and *olhar* as in 21:2.

options.label: afasteis de mim … atendei à minha defesa
options.note: The stylist and MS1932; *afastar* is discédere's in 21:11, *atender* is inténdere's (D3).

decisions.latin: Érue a frámea, Deus, ánimam meam
decisions.why: éruere: 13 lines (grep), almost always with a source named (*de, a, ab*). Its Greek (ῥῦσαι) is the verb behind liberáre and erípere too, but the Latin keeps three verbs, and 36:40 sets *liberábit … éruet* side by side, so it cannot be *livrar*. *arrancar* (the glossary's erípere with a source) fits éruere's own sense, "pluck out" (L&S), and a source is named here; the two never stand in one verse. frámea → espada (glossary).

options.label: Arrancai
options.note: Ruling: the plucking out, with a source named.

options.label: Livrai
options.note: MS1932; liberáre's verb (21:5).

options.label: Libertai
options.note: erípere's verb without a source (21:9).

decisions.why: The Latin's substantive feminine (τὴν μονογενῆ μου), parallel to *ánimam meam*: my only one — my soul, my life. 34:17 *a leónibus únicam meam* is the twin (grep). Kept bare, as DRB (*my only one*) and MS1932 (*a minha única*, with a gloss). Heard (draft 1): the stylist found the proparoxytone *única* weak at the final and moved the object forward (*e a minha única, da mão do cão*); taken — order only (D2), the parallel with *a minha alma* still heard. The blind reader heard "my only soul" first, "my only life" second, and a beloved woman third — the Latin's openness.

options.label: a minha única
options.note: Ruling: as open as the Latin.

options.label: a minha única vida
options.note: MS1932's gloss in the text; explains.

decisions.why: unicórnis → *unicórnio*, the Latin's (and Greek's μονόκερως) animal — 28:6, 77:69, 91:11 (grep); not the Hebrew's wild ox. cornu → chifre (glossary). humílitas: the glossary row (open) has *humilhação* (9:14, 118:50 — being brought low). Here it is the object to be SAVED, a metonymy for the lowly self like *únicam meam*: *salvai … a minha humilhação* would be heard as saving (keeping) the humiliation, and *leão … humilhação* rhymes at mediant and final, which the Latin does not (rule 5). So *a minha pequenez* (DRB *my lowness*) — a local departure from the row, for these two reasons.

options.label: unicórnios … a minha pequenez
options.note: Ruling: DRB's lowness; no rhyme, no wrong hearing.

options.label: … a minha humilhação
options.note: The row; rhymes with *leão*, and *salvai a humilhação* misleads.

options.label: … a minha humildade
options.note: MS1932; heard as the virtue.

decisions.latin: semen Jacob … semen Israël … semen meum
decisions.why: semen → descendência (settled, D32, which names 21:24 *semen Jacob*: *semente de Jacó* is heard as seed). No plant image in these verses. MS1932 *descendência / posteridade*.

options.label: descendência
options.note: Ruling: D32.

options.label: semente
options.note: DRB *seed*; the image kept, heard as grain.

decisions.why: The stylist heard *louvai-o … glorificai-o* rhyme at both cadences and moved the vocative last. Refused: the rhyme is the Latin's own (*laudáte eum … glorificáte eum*, rule 5's exception), and the Latin puts the vocative first in both cola.

options.label: the Latin's order
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's order and echo.

options.label: glorificai-o, toda a …
options.note: The stylist: no rhyme; the cadence on *Jacó*.

decisions.latin: non sprevit, neque despéxit deprecatiónem páuperis
decisions.why: spérnere → desprezar (glossary), and it answers 21:7 *o desprezo* (one Greek root, ἐξουδεν-). despícere with God as subject → desdenhar (glossary row, 9:22). deprecátio → prece (glossary, proposed for settling: 6:10, 16:1a, 118:169).

options.label: desdenhou … prece
options.note: Ruling: the two rows.

options.label: rejeitou … súplica
options.note: rejeitar is reprobáre's; súplica the deprecátio row's option.

decisions.latin: Apud te laus mea in ecclésia magna
decisions.why: apud te: with you, in your keeping (DRB *With thee is my praise*). The Greek is παρὰ σοῦ, "from you" — the Latin's preposition is followed. The line is verbless; *está* supplied. réddere vota → *pagar os votos* (glossary row *réddere*, names 21:26).

options.label: Junto de vós está
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's *apud*.

options.label: De vós vem
options.note: The Greek's παρὰ σοῦ; not the Latin.

options.label: A vós se dirigirá
options.note: MS1932; a verb and a direction the Latin lacks.

decisions.latin: vivent corda eórum in sǽculum sǽculi
decisions.why: in sǽculum sǽculi → pelos séculos dos séculos (settled, D27). The stylist asked for the formula first, so that the verse does not close on the proparoxytone *séculos*. Refused: the Latin itself closes on *sǽculi*; the formula closes verses so everywhere (18:10, 20:5, 20:7, held the same way); and the Latin puts *vivent* first. The Latinist asked again (minor) for *pelo século do século* — refused, D27.

options.label: the Latin's order

forms.v27b: viverão os seus corações pelos séculos dos séculos

options.note: Ruling: the Latin's order; D27's words.

options.label: formula first

forms.v27b: pelos séculos dos séculos viverão os seus corações

options.note: The stylist: a stressed final syllable.

decisions.latin: in conspéctu timéntium eum … in conspéctu ejus … in conspéctu ejus
decisions.why: in conspéctu (glossary row, open): the Ps 17 evidence splits it — *à vista de* where it is the place something is seen, *na sua presença* where it goes with an act. 21:26 the vows paid in the sight of witnesses → *à vista*; 21:28b the nations worship and 21:30 they fall down → *na sua presença* (MS1932 both).

options.label: à vista … na sua presença ×2
options.note: Ruling: the row's two renderings, by build.

options.label: à vista ×3
options.note: One rendering for one Latin phrase; *adorarão à vista dele* is stiff.

decisions.why: convértere → voltar, with D25's one exception: *converter* where men turn to God — the ends of the earth turning to the Lord is that sense (DRB *converted*, MS1932 *converter-se-ão*). *Hão de lembrar-se e converter-se* for two futures that mesóclise would make heavy (*Lembrar-se-ão e converter-se-ão*).

options.label: converter-se
options.note: Ruling: D25's exception.

options.label: voltar-se
options.note: The row's verb; loses the conversion.

decisions.why: pinguis → gordo (glossary, names 21:30): the concrete image (rule 5; D2) — the fat ones of the earth, the prosperous. MS1932 *os ricos* explains. It echoes 21:13 *tauri pingues* → *touros gordos*.

options.label: gordos
options.note: Ruling: the image, and the echo of 21:13.

options.label: ricos
options.note: MS1932; the sense named, the image lost.

decisions.latin: pópulo qui nascétur, quem fecit Dóminus
decisions.why: The Latin's relative *quem* (whom the Lord made), the people's; Rahlfs's Greek has ὅτι ἐποίησεν ὁ κύριος ("that the Lord has done") — the Latin is followed, and so is its *cæli*, which Rahlfs's text lacks. Two relatives stacked, as the Latin. MS1932 *e que o Senhor formou*.

options.label: que o Senhor fez
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's relative, subject after the verb avoided so that *o Senhor* is heard as subject.

options.label: o qual o Senhor fez
options.note: The antecedent made unmistakable; heavier.

choices.21:2: The cry of the Passion. Mt 27:46 / Mk 15:34 (Clementine, fetched) have *Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me?* — not the psalm's wording; the psalm keeps its own. Second colon verbless in the Latin; *estão* supplied.
choices.21:3: exáudies → escutareis (D3), no object, as the Latin.
choices.21:4: *laus Israël* in apposition to *Tu*, vocative without *ó* (the glossary's rule for bare vocatives).
choices.21:5: speráre in → esperar em; liberáre → livrar; the Latin's doubled *speravérunt* kept.
choices.21:8: *vidéntes* present participle with a perfect → *os que me viam*.
choices.21:9: The mockers' words stand unmarked, as in the Latin; *ele* named so that *que ele o liberte* is heard as a wish, not a relative.
choices.21:10: The verse carries a third sentence after the second colon (*In te projéctus sum ex útero:*) — reproduced after it, as DO does.
choices.21:14: rápere → arrebatar, rugíre → rugir (glossary); *os suum* singular → *a sua boca*.
choices.21:15: Keyed 21:15 (DO's first line of the repeated id). effúndere → derramar. The Latin's order *Sicut aqua effúsus sum* kept — it is also good Portuguese.
choices.21:15b: Keyed 21:15b: DO gives this line the id 21:15 again (see ids.py).
choices.21:16: dedúcere in púlverem → *fazer descer ao pó* (D25, which names 21:16).
choices.21:17: Keyed 21:17 (DO's first line of the repeated id).
choices.21:17b: Keyed 21:17b: DO's second 21:17. dinumeráre → contar (3 lines: 89:11, 138:18).
choices.21:18: DO's 21:18 holds Vulgate vv. 18b–19 (there is no 21:19 line). The second colon is Mt 27:35's quotation word for word (Clementine, fetched) — formula row proposed.
choices.21:20: *Tu autem, Dómine* → *Mas vós, Senhor*, as 21:4 *Tu autem* → *Mas vós*.
choices.21:23: Heb 2:12 (Clementine, fetched) quotes it as *Nuntiabo nomen tuum fratribus meis: in medio ecclesiæ laudabo te* — *Nuntiabo* for the psalm's *Narrábo*; the psalm keeps narráre → narrar (glossary).
choices.21:24: Plural human addressees → *vós* (decided); *louvai-o*, *glorificai-o* are safe imperatives.
choices.21:25: Keyed 21:25 (DO's first line of the repeated id).
choices.21:25b: Keyed 21:25b: DO's second 21:25. *avértere fáciem … a me* → *desviar de mim a sua face* (the glossary formula, 12:1); exaudívit → escutou (D3); *clamárem ad eum* → *clamava a ele*.
choices.21:27: saturáre → saciar, passive (glossary, names 21:27); requírere → procurar (glossary, 13:2); in sǽculum sǽculi → pelos séculos dos séculos (D27).
choices.21:28: Keyed 21:28 (DO's first line of the repeated id). fines terræ → os confins da terra (glossary).
choices.21:28b: Keyed 21:28b: DO's second 21:28. famíliæ géntium → *as famílias das nações*.
choices.21:29: Built as the formula *Dómini est salus* → *Do Senhor é a salvação* (3:9). dominári + genitive → *dominar* + object (glossary, 18:14b).
choices.21:30: manducáre and edere (21:27) both → *comer* (one Greek verb, φαγ-). *cadent* → *cairão*, nothing added.
choices.21:32: *generátio ventúra* → *a geração que há de vir*; *qui nascétur* → *que nascerá* (two futures, two forms, as the Latin varies participle and verb).

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm21.txt, 34 prayed lines. DO repeats four ids (21:15, 21:17, 21:25, 21:28) — the first psalm to do so (ps021/dup_ids.py lists 57 psalms that do); the shared scripts key verses by id and cannot hold two lines under one, so the second line of each is keyed with the suffix b and the shared render/checks/site are run through ps021/run.py, which swaps latin.readVerses for ps021/ids.py's (shared files untouched). DO's 21:18 is Vulgate 18b–19 (no 21:19 line). Collated against the Clementine Vulgate fetched from Bolls (consult/bolls-VULG-19-21.json): identical wording. NT places fetched and read (ps021/show_vulg.py): Mt 27:35 = 21:18's second colon word for word; Mt 27:39 *moventes capita sua*; Mt 27:43 *confidit in Deo: liberet nunc, si vult eum* (not the psalm's wording); Mt 27:46 / Mk 15:34 *Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me?* (not the psalm's wording); Jn 19:24 *Partiti sunt vestimenta mea sibi: et in vestem meam miserunt sortem* (another wording); Heb 2:12 *Nuntiabo nomen tuum fratribus meis: in medio ecclesiæ laudabo te* (*Nuntiabo* for *Narrábo*). Hetzenauer print read not done.

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps021.md (LXX, Hebrew, Douay-Rheims, Matos Soares 1932 text layer; no Diurnal for this psalm; DO's Portuguese not used, D12). Repeats checked with ps005/grep_latin.py: ecclési- (10 lines), concíli- (4), synagóg- (4), éru- (13), fód- (3), elong- (6), vítul- (7), obsid- (2), únic-/unicórn-, úter- (6), dinumer- (3), manduc- (9); Greek of concílium / ecclésia read at 1:5, 25:4–5, 25:12, 39:10–11 (parallels generated for Pss 1, 25, 39). L&S read for fodio. Septuagintal readings kept against the Hebrew: 21:2 *as palavras das minhas faltas*, 21:3 *e não para a minha insensatez*, 21:13 *novilhos*, 21:17b *Perfuraram* (not "like a lion"), 21:21 *a minha única*, 21:22 *unicórnios*, 21:27 *os seus corações*, 21:30 *comeram e adoraram*, 21:31 *a minha alma viverá para ele*. Where the Latin differs from Rahlfs's Greek it is followed: 21:2 *réspice* (πρόσχες), 21:26 *apud* (παρὰ σοῦ), 21:32 *cæli* and *quem* (ὅτι). 37 decisions.

Draft 1 through ps021/run.py checks: hard pass (exit 0). One flag mended before the critics: 21:22 *leão … humilhação* rhymed at mediant and final → *a minha pequenez* (decision `humilitatem`). Soft flags accepted: 21:2 first colon −3; 21:6 second +3 (*envergonhados*, D15); 21:8 first +3; 21:9 second −5 (*porque o quer*: the Latin's three words); 21:10 second colon +10 — it carries the verse's third sentence (*In te projéctus sum ex útero*), and *o seio materno* (see decision `uberibus`); 21:15b +4 (*que se derrete*); 21:16 first +3; 21:17 first −3; 21:17b second −4; 21:20 first −3; 21:25 second −4; 21:26 first +4 (*está* supplied); 21:27 second +3 (D27); 21:31 first +3. Rhymes that are the Latin's own echo, kept (rule 5): 21:24 *louvai-o / glorificai-o* (*laudáte eum / glorificáte eum*), 21:30 *terra / terra* (*terræ / terram*), 21:28b / 21:29 *nações / nações* (*géntium / géntium*).

Draft 1. Three minors, no major; the marks confirmed in all 34 verses. «A tradução conserva o conteúdo latino, inclusive suas imagens e construções incomuns; os reparos encontrados são menores e dizem respeito à conservação estrita do número.» One taken, two refused.

outcomes.remark: minor: 'o peito' singular for the plural ubéribus → 'os seios da minha mãe'
outcomes.reason: The plural taken as MS1932 has it, *os peitos*: *os seios* beside *o seio materno* would be heard as one thing.

outcomes.remark: minor: 'lançaram sortes' pluralises sortem → 'lançaram a sorte'
outcomes.reason: *lançar a sorte* is heard as casting one's fate; *lançar sortes* is the idiom for drawing lots, and the blind reader heard it so. Number is grammar (D2).

outcomes.remark: minor: 'pelos séculos dos séculos' pluralises → 'pelo século do século'
outcomes.reason: Settled, D27.

audit.note: Draft 1. Eight verses; best 21:5, worst 21:3. «O salmo tem gravidade e boa sustentação oral … os tropeços mais definidos estão nas palavras proparoxítonas colocadas nas cadências.» Four taken (21:3 in part, 21:12, 21:16 with the glossary row's own option, 21:21), four refused and kept as options (21:14, 21:20, 21:24, 21:27).

outcomes.remark: (worst line) the ellipses leave the voice without support → 'e de noite, e isso não será para minha insensatez'
outcomes.reason: The copula *será* taken (grammar, D2) — it also mends the blind reader's *para* = *parar*; his *isso* left out (+2 syllables); his whole line is option 3.

outcomes.remark: 'próxima' proparoxytone at the mediant → 'está perto'
outcomes.reason: The plainer of two faithful words; answers the psalm's *longe*.

outcomes.remark: 'Abriram sobre mim' sounds a translated spatial build → 'contra mim'
outcomes.reason: *abrir a boca contra* is to speak against; *sobre mim* keeps the lion's jaws over the prey (MS1932 has it). The Latinist passed it.

outcomes.remark: 'se apegou' is affection before touch → 'ficou presa'
outcomes.reason: Taken in substance with the adhǽrére row's own option, *se colou* (DM1962): the physical sticking, still one verb for one; his *ficou presa* (a state) is option 3.

outcomes.remark: 'não ponhais longe' sounds assembled → 'não afasteis de mim'
outcomes.reason: *afastar* is discédere's in 21:11; the Latin's *longe* (answering 21:2 and 21:12) would be lost.

outcomes.remark: 'única' proparoxytone at the final → 'e a minha única, da mão do cão'
outcomes.reason: Order only (D2).

outcomes.remark: rhyme 'louvai-o … glorificai-o' → vocative last
outcomes.reason: The Latin's own echo (*laudáte eum … glorificáte eum*), rule 5's exception; the Latin's order.

outcomes.remark: the proparoxytone 'séculos' at the final → formula first
outcomes.reason: The Latin closes on *sǽculi* too; held so at 18:10, 20:5, 20:7.

audit.note: Draft 1. 38 items, 7 unknown words (escarneceram, novilhos, sitiaram, arrebata, sitiou, fitaram, confins). Two wrong first hearings, both mended in draft 2 (21:3 *para* heard as *parar*; 21:4 *louvor de Israel* heard as the holy place's name); *novilhos* replaced. The rest are the Latin's own openness or its images, kept.

outcomes.remark: 'não para a minha insensatez' heard first as 'my folly does not stop' (parar)
outcomes.reason: *não será para* — after the copula *para* is the preposition.

outcomes.remark: 'louvor de Israel' heard as a name of the holy place
outcomes.reason: *vós, louvor de Israel*: the subject named again, heard as God.

outcomes.remark: 'novilhos' unknown
outcomes.reason: *bezerros*, the plainer faithful word.

outcomes.remark: 'porque o quer' heard as 'because the Lord wants to save him'
outcomes.reason: Near the Latin's sense (he wills him / delights in him); *porque lhe quer bem* stays the option — it adds *bem*.

outcomes.remark: 'os gordos da terra' heard first as people with fat bodies
outcomes.reason: The Latin's image (rule 5), and 21:13 *touros gordos* echoes it; the sense (the prosperous) came second. *os ricos* (MS1932) is the option.

outcomes.remark: 'escarneceram' unknown
outcomes.reason: The glossary keeps *escarnecer* for derídere, *zombar* for subsannáre; a standard Bible word.

outcomes.remark: 'sitiaram' / 21:17 'sitiou' unknown
outcomes.reason: The plain word for a siege; *cercar* is circumdáre's in the same two verses; *assediar* is heard as harassment.

outcomes.remark: 'arrebata' unknown
outcomes.reason: rápere → arrebatar (glossary, working).

outcomes.remark: 'fitaram' unknown
outcomes.reason: inspícere, only here: *fitar* is the stare (DRB); *examinar* is examináre's and *encarar* confrontation. Kept; the next reader will show whether it holds.

outcomes.remark: 'confins' unknown
outcomes.reason: fines terræ → os confins da terra (glossary).

outcomes.remark: 'a minha única' — my only soul / my only life / a beloved woman
outcomes.reason: The Latin's own openness; heard first as the soul, which is the sense.

outcomes.remark: 'a minha pequenez' heard as my fragility
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly; no change.

audit.note: v2: 21:3 *e não será para a minha insensatez* (the stylist's copula; mends *para* = *parar*); 21:4 *vós, louvor de Israel* (the blind reader); 21:10 *os peitos* (the Latinist's plural); 21:12 *está perto* (the stylist); 21:13 *bezerros* (the blind reader); 21:16 *se colou* (the stylist, with the glossary row's option); 21:21 *e a minha única, da mão do cão* (the stylist's order). New decisions: laus, proxima, super, adhaesit, glorificate, saeculi (the last four hold refused stylist lines as options). Draft 1 kept as prayed.v1.json.

The gate, on draft 2. No major; the two minors he gave draft 1 and that were refused, repeated; the marks confirmed in all 34 verses. «A tradução conserva o conteúdo latino, com duas alterações de número em expressões convencionais.» Every change of draft 2 (21:3, 21:4, 21:10, 21:12, 21:13, 21:16, 21:21) passed without remark. The stylist and the blind reader read draft 1 only.

outcomes.remark: minor (again): 'lançaram sortes' → 'lançaram a sorte'
outcomes.reason: As on draft 1: the idiom; *lançar a sorte* is heard as casting one's fate.

outcomes.remark: minor (again): 'pelos séculos dos séculos' → 'pelo século do século'
